outcome: Keep an evidence snapshot's row position apart from the imported cells, found in the Sonnet review of PR 18: an imported column named row overwrote the position in the stored values
criteria: Each entry of an evidence reference's values is {"row": position, "cells": {column: value}}, so importing rows [{"row": "A", "v": 1}, {"row": "B", "v": 2}, {"row": "C", "v": 3}] with evidence rows [2] stores [{"row": 2, "cells": {"row": "C", "v": 3}}], in the import response and in get_provenance

A regression test covers a column named row, existing evidence tests use the new shape, README.md and the EvidenceRef docstring describe it, the backend test suite passes, and the fix is committed and pushed to feat/issue-17

dispositions.note: 510 backend tests pass; the landing commit carries this outcome and is pushed to feat/issue-17 right after this close

note: _evidence_values now builds each snapshot entry as {row, cells}. Six evidence test assertions were moved to that shape, and test_a_column_named_row_does_not_hide_the_position covers the import response and get_provenance. README.md and the EvidenceRef docstring show the shape. The Sonnet review's other three points (per-position queries in rows_at, no shape repair beside a failing check, no basename fallback for a missing path) were left as they are with the user's agreement.
